payload.task: Li-ion self-diffusion coefficient (self_diffusion, cm2/s) in pristine crystalline LiF by molecular dynamics
payload.reason: Premise check failed: the requested quantity is not well-defined/measurable with this setup. (1) In a pristine (defect-free) rock-salt LiF crystal, Li transport needs vacancies or interstitials, and a perfect periodic MD cell contains none. Spontaneous Frenkel/Schottky formation costs several eV, so the equilibrium defect fraction below the melting point (~1121 K) is tiny (order 1e-6 or less), meaning a 10^3-10^4-atom cell on a ns timescale is expected to contain zero defects. The Li MSD then just plateaus at the vibrational amplitude, so the true MD answer is 'below the detection limit' (D << ~1e-8 cm2/s for ns runs), not a number. Fitting a slope to that plateau gives a spurious value. (2) Any measurable D from such a run would come from an artefact: a superheated/melting or mechanically unstable crystal, or an MLIP outside its domain at high T. Either would mean reporting liquid or artefact diffusion as crystal diffusion. (3) The request gives no temperature, and D in an ionic crystal is strongly Arrhenius, so a single value is underspecified. (4) Validation: no independent measured diffusion reference for LiF (or any ionic-crystal diffusivity) is in /data/calibration/tier1.json (it holds melting points, latent heats, densities and conductivities of PCMs and metals), and I will not invent one, so the required independent check of the diffusion protocol cannot be met here. PROPOSED WELL-POSED ALTERNATIVE: Well-posed alternatives I can run on request: (a) Li vacancy-mediated diffusion: insert a known vacancy (or Schottky pair with charge compensation), run NVT MD at several T below Tm (e.g. 700-1050 K, several ns, multiple seeds), and report D_vac(T), migration barrier E_m from an Arrhenius fit, and the defect concentration used. Then D_Li = c_v * D_vac * f (correlation factor f≈0.78 for fcc), with c_v stated explicitly (intrinsic from a computed Schottky formation energy, or extrinsic/doping-controlled). (b) Static NEB for the Li-vacancy hop barrier with the same MLIP, as a cross-check of E_m. (c) Validation first: recover LiF's measured melting point (~1121 K) with a solid-liquid coexistence run using the same model, and the lattice constant/density, before trusting any transport number. Uncertainty would cover seed-to-seed scatter, MSD-fit window and finite-size effects, but not systematic MLIP error beyond what (c) bounds.
